assessments.summary: Relative to the accepted 30-row definitions and optimization order, the report establishes exact at-most-N-output reduction on finite posterior grids, the reflection-closed reduction for reflected receiver pairs, both Q0 infima equal to c, the coercive floor B(G,K) >= V_0(g,k) >= max{F(g),F(k)}, and the resulting midpoint window when c <= U < 2c.
scopeQualifications: Validity is conditional on the accepted private-message 30-row outer-bound premise and definitions in the cited transaction.
The receiver reductions apply to finite-output, binary-input, input-only receivers and finite grids Q containing {0,1/2,1}.
The reflected reduction applies only when Q is reflection closed and only within the class (m,m^circ); it does not establish arbitrary-pair symmetrization or full-functional reflected optimality.
The Q0 conclusions are sampled finite-grid statements and do not establish continuum cardinality bounds, limit interchange, or an unconditional capacity converse.
The coercivity bounds are necessary conditions derived from B(G,K) <= U, not sufficient conditions or a benchmark improvement.
evidenceIssues: The underlying 30-row outer-bound premise is imported from the cited transaction rather than independently established in this record; no further proof defect is reported.
